sentences.text: Shri Mohan Lal Patidar - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Bhuwan Gautam - Govt. Advocate for the respondent N None present for the victim/respondent No.2, though served.
I.A. No.9376/2024, an application for urgent hearing is taken up, considered and allowed.
Heard on I.A. No.16393/2023, which is an application filed under Section 389 (1) of Cr.P.C for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
The appellant Anarsingh has been convicted under Section 376 of IPC and sentenced to suffer twelve years RI with fine of Rs.2,000/- with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that this is a case of consent.
Prosecutrix is a major lady aged around 45 years.
There is no DNA report and even in medical report, no injury has been found on the body of the prosecutrix.
Final hearing of this appeal is not possible in near future therefore, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended and they may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer of the appellant stating that the trial Court has convicted the appellant and did not appreciate the evidence on record.
Testimony of prosecutrix is also supported by the statement of her husband (PW-2).
No case of suspension is made out.
Therefore, application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail be dismissed.
2 CRA-10545-2023 We have heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, when no injury has been found on the body of the prosecutrix, no DNA report has been obtained, offence under Section 506 of IPC threatening by wielding axe has not been found proved, the application I.A. No.16393/2023 is allowed and the jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended.
